There have been quite a few discussions in the tech industry in the past few years about how ineffective the typical technical interview is at gauging true competency. What are your thoughts on this? What do you think can be improved about the system?

I think it's necessary. There are too many universities out there offering bullshit degrees. A simple coding test from an advanced algorithms class should be sufficient to determine basic knowledge, in lieu of a professional exam that other branches of engineering have. It should not be the only test. This is not to say that things do not get out of hand. One time I had a battery of five very hard questions from leetcode for a research engineer position.

Thank you for your perspective! While I agree that some sort of examination is necessary, what are your opinions on an alternative interviewing technique? For example, what if, for example, a company is hiring a data scientist, and they give a candidate a toy dataset and a problem, and give them the day to use whatever libraries and tools they find most comfortable to come up with the best solution to that problem?
